clue.text: Lose extremely sharp spike on motorway

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities of the next word, its first and last letters only

parts.note: the two ends of the word
to lace or spike a drink is to add alcohol to it

explanation.surface: A driver loses a tyre to a vicious metal spike lying on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the sharp spike after the motorway in this across entry. The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: To misplace something is to mislay it, a near synonym of losing it.

clue.text: Leaves untouched

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a herb grown for its aromatic leaves
second meaning: as new, in perfect condition

explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb, as if someone departs; it is the noun, the foliage of a herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Mint is a herb used for its leaves, and an item in mint condition is pristine and unused.

clue.text: Perhaps foil spies or scammers?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a foil is one example of a fencing blade
second meaning, read cryptically: each of these is a word starting with S

explanation.walkthrough: 'foil' looks like the verb to thwart, as if catching crooks; it is the fencing weapon. The question mark flags the playful reading of the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: A foil is a light fencing weapon, an example of a blade; spies and scammers are both words beginning with S.

clue.text: Watch where you go with leader of killers freed

parts.note: a loo is a toilet, where one goes when needing to

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front, so only its opening letter counts

explanation.surface: A warning to keep an eye on where you walk now that the head of a murderous gang has been released.
explanation.walkthrough: Loo is everyday British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A lookout is a watch, a person or post keeping guard and observing.

clue.text: Fatty things, roughly two on each of us

parts.note: c is short for circa, Latin for about or roughly
every person has a pair of hips

explanation.surface: A rueful remark about the fatty bulges each of us carries, roughly two per person.
explanation.walkthrough: Chips are British fried potato strips, fries.
explanation.definitionFit: Chips are deep-fried potato, a notoriously fatty food item.

clue.text: Shopkeeper oddly voided voucher, I'm mad about it

indicators.note: about means going round, so the exclamation wraps around what came before

parts.note: the growl of an angry person

indicators.note: voided means emptied, so the letters in odd positions are thrown away and the even ones stay

explanation.surface: A customer fumes over a coupon that was cancelled at the till.
explanation.walkthrough: A growl of rage is the crossword's usual way to write 'I'm mad'; 'voided' here means emptied rather than cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: A grocer is a shopkeeper who sells food and household goods.

clue.text: Finery on girl, hair barely done up

indicators.note: barely suggests stripped bare, so the word loses its outer letters

parts.note: an informal word for a girl

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from the bottom, in the opposite direction

parts.note: the inner letters once both ends go

explanation.surface: A girl dressed in her finest with her hair hastily pinned up.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia is ceremonial dress and emblems, splendid clothing or finery.

clue.text: Rapport is shot after cold interruption

indicators.note: after puts the 'is shot' pair behind the cold interruption, so that pair comes second

parts.note: a hem is a small cough made to interrupt or attract attention
to have a shot is to have a try

explanation.surface: A relationship is ruined after one partner coldly cuts in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the 'is shot' part behind the cold interruption. 'Shot' looks like an anagram signal but is simply an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemistry between people is a natural rapport or mutual attraction.

clue.text: In which one regards blossoms

indicators.note: to blossom is to develop and open out, so the preceding letters unfold into a new form

explanation.surface: A description of a place where people admire the flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: it is both the wordplay and a description of a garden where one looks at flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose garden is a planted area where visitors admire roses in bloom.

clue.text: New word energy in ol' Mog's anagrams

indicators.note: the setter declares outright that the material is to be rearranged into another word

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophes

explanation.surface: The setter Mog boasts of inventing new words through anagrams.
explanation.walkthrough: Mog is this puzzle's setter, so the surface is a wry self-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: A neologism is a newly coined term or expression.

clue.text: Mystery vehicle lifts skyward mid-race

indicators.note: mid places the preceding letters in the middle of the following word

parts.note: the mile is a classic running race

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up toward the sky means reading the letters bottom to top

explanation.surface: A puzzling sight: a car taking off into the air in the middle of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: Medieval mystery plays were also called miracle plays, which makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Mystery and miracle both name the medieval religious dramas, and a miracle is something inexplicable.

clue.text: Reckon inn's patrons must have time out

indicators.note: having something out means it is removed, here the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An innkeeper's view that customers deserve a break.
explanation.definitionFit: To reckon or guess is to estimate or suppose without certainty.

clue.text: Pique about son caught streaming bad habit online

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for pique is read backwards

parts.note: to be in a mood is to be in a fit of pique

explanation.surface: Annoyance about a child glued to a streaming service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'streaming' suggests online video, but it means flowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Doomscrolling is the compulsive scrolling through grim news on a phone, a modern internet vice.

clue.text: Snack is crumbly, but it is ace

indicators.note: something crumbly falls to bits, so the letters break up and re-form

parts.words: is crumbly, but it is ace
parts.note: the letters of 'is', 'but it' and 'ace', with the second 'is' joining

explanation.surface: A snack may crumble, but it is still excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumbly' sits inside the fodder; the second 'is' only links fodder to fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea biscuit is a light snack, typically a cookie eaten with a cuppa.

clue.text: Applaud retired singer kicking butt

indicators.note: the butt is the tail end, so kicking it off drops the final letter

parts.note: a singer with a low female or high male voice

explanation.surface: Cheers for a retired vocalist who is still tough and feisty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kicking butt' reads as slang for being aggressive, but literally removes a tail letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To exalt is to praise highly, to glorify, close in sense to applauding.

clue.text: Cooked for culinary tool White

parts.note: à la, as in a dish cooked in the style of or for someone
a bulb syringe for moistening roasting meat

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget, cooked up for a cook, in white.
explanation.walkthrough: Menu phrases like 'à la king' name a dish prepared for or in the manner of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a pale mineral, and the word is used as an adjective for a smooth pure white.

clue.text: Casting expert put in to secure HK film star

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: to enter data is to put it in
Jackie Chan, Hong Kong action star

explanation.surface: A casting director brought in to sign a Hong Kong film star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casting' suggests film auditions; here it means casting spells.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchanter is a sorcerer, someone skilled at casting spells.

clue.text: Blunder with introduction of see-through runner's things?

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so only the word's first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A clumsy mistake involving a runner's transparent kit.
explanation.walkthrough: An errand boy is a 'runner', so errands are what a runner runs.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand runner carries out errands, so errands are a runner's tasks.

clue.text: Bar supporters, mostly where Juventus play

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: Serie A is Italy's top football division

explanation.surface: Football fans barred from a stadium, as with Juventus supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporters' suggests football fans, which Juventus encourages; they are undergarments.
explanation.definitionFit: A brasserie is an informal restaurant or bar serving drinks and food.

clue.text: Mushy peas, barely cooked, on a fork?

indicators.note: mushy means pulped and softened, so the word's letters are mashed into another order

parts.note: meat cooked only barely is still red inside

explanation.surface: Mushy peas and rare meat, picked up on a fork.
explanation.walkthrough: Mushy peas are a British side dish of mashed marrowfat peas, usually eaten with fish and chips.
explanation.definitionFit: Food speared is pierced with a pointed implement, as on a fork's tines.

clue.text: This guy finishing what was once your herb

parts.note: the speaker, the guy writing this

explanation.surface: Someone speaks of an old-fashioned herb that was once yours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This guy' is the setter's way of saying me; 'finishing' puts it at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is a common culinary herb with small aromatic leaves.

clue.text: Crime ultimately without motive

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so the final letter alone is kept

parts.note: a motive is a reason for acting

explanation.surface: A crime that in the end turns out to have had no motive.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the crime of betraying one's country or sovereign.

clue.text: Remix a Spencer Davis hit from the late 70s

indicators.note: a remix reworks a recording, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A remix of a 1960s Spencer Davis Group song becomes a late-70s chart hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spencer Davis Group was a 1960s British band, so 'hit' suggests a record; it is an arcade game.
explanation.definitionFit: Space Invaders, released in 1978, was a hugely successful arcade video game.

clue.text: Pose as an American

parts.note: standard abbreviation; that the letters also run unbroken through these three words is a coincidence of the charade

explanation.surface: An instruction to pretend to be from the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pose as' looks like one phrase meaning impersonate; split it and 'Pose' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An asana is a yoga posture or position held during practice.

clue.text: Head of spatula pounds molluscs

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so only the opening letter counts

parts.note: British slang for pounds sterling, plural unchanged

explanation.surface: A cook hammers shellfish with the end of a spatula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pounds' looks like a verb for bashing; it is money. The plural of squid can be squid, so it matches molluscs.
explanation.definitionFit: Squid are cephalopods, a class of marine molluscs with tentacles.

clue.text: Grow significantly more when taking mineral

indicators.note: taking here means taking away, subtracting one thing from the phrase

parts.note: far more means a great deal more
rock from which a mineral is extracted

explanation.surface: A plant grows much more when given a mineral supplement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' suggests absorbing a mineral, but it means subtracting.
explanation.definitionFit: To farm crops or livestock is to grow or raise them.

clue.text: Rank mouth

definitions.meaning: first meaning: complete, out-and-out, as in rank stupidity

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank mouth' suggests bad breath; both words are definitions, an adjective and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter as an adjective means absolute, like rank; as a verb it means to voice words.

clue.text: Rudely ask shah to import UK egg dish

indicators.note: to import is to bring inside, so the letters take another piece into them
doing something rudely means roughly, without care, so the letters get knocked about

explanation.surface: A demand that a shah bring in British produce, made impolitely.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakshuka is a North African and Middle Eastern dish of eggs poached in spiced tomato sauce.

clue.text: Exchange without one outburst

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one word is wrapped around the other

explanation.surface: An angry outburst at a deal falling through without anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech, a verbal outburst.

clue.text: Canonisation isn't occasion to get into kinky stuff

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it, so these words are enclosed

parts.note: a do is a party or social occasion

explanation.surface: A pious protest that sainthood is no excuse for wild behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Saintdom is the state of being a saint, which canonisation confers.
